name: Canisters failing: a source term with barriers, and two disruptive events
description: 4,500 spent-fuel canisters in a repository. None fails before year 1,000; after that the failures follow a Weibull with a characteristic life of 50,000 years and a shape of 2, the corrosion form. When a canister fails, 3% of its caesium and 0.5% of the rest is in the water at once (the instant release fraction) and the remainder waits for the fuel matrix, which dissolves at one part in ten million a year. The release goes into the near-field water, which is flushed to the geosphere; switch the mass-balance audit on under SIMULATION to watch the bookkeeping close. Two disruptive events act on it: an earthquake, a Poisson process at 2e-5 a year that fails 5% of the still-intact canisters at each occurrence, and a glaciation at 100,000 years that strips 80% of the biosphere out of the model. A deterministic run takes the earthquake in its expected-value form; a probabilistic run draws its occurrences — compare the staircase of Quake with its expected line.

parameters.name: t_first_failure
parameters.comment: No canister fails before this: the time the earliest corrosion process could breach one.

parameters.name: canister_life
parameters.comment: The Weibull scale: 63% of the canisters have failed one life after the first failure.

parameters.name: matrix_rate
parameters.comment: The fraction of the exposed fuel matrix dissolving per year. Everything bound in it leaves congruently.

parameters.name: flush_rate
parameters.comment: Turnover of the near-field water: the fraction leaving for the geosphere per year.

parameters.name: geo_rate
parameters.comment: Transit through the geosphere to the biosphere, as a first-order rate.

parameters.name: quake_rate
parameters.comment: Earthquakes breaching canisters: one in fifty thousand years.

parameters.name: t_glacial
parameters.comment: When the next ice sheet reaches the site.

waste_packages.name: Canisters
waste_packages.comment: The source term: the inventory starts inside the canisters and reaches the water only as they fail and the fuel dissolves. What leaves is the line drawn out of the block.

compartments.name: NearField
compartments.comment: The water in and around the failed canisters. A solubility limit would go on the transfer out of here, as an availability.

transfers.name: Release
transfers.comment: What leaves the canisters. Its rate is the block itself, so there is nothing to set.

transfers.name: Loss
transfers.comment: Dilution and dispersal out of the modelled biosphere.

events.name: Quake
events.comment: An earthquake: at each occurrence 5% of the canisters still intact fail. Deterministically a hazard of 1e-6 a year on the intact inventory; in a probabilistic run, drawn occurrences.

events.name: Glaciation
events.comment: The ice sheet arrives: 80% of what the biosphere holds is scraped away, out of the model.
